name: alfred-nathan-house

building.title: Alfred Nathan House, University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 103's outline from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; used only to choose the crop box, to pick the building's own points (frame.near_outline) and to draw on the heightmap figure; the frame comes from the LiDAR.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: view frame: the foot of the house's front steps, on the porch's centre line (parts/house.js, MEASURED.house.porch); the LiDAR ground on the path there is 45.72-45.78 m, so ground is 45.75 and the model's y is 0 there; place.py puts it on the map

lidar.licence: Auckland Part 1 LiDAR (2024), OpenTopography NZ24_Auckland, doi:10.5069/G9HH6H8T: sourced from LINZ and licensed by Regional Software Holdings Limited for re-use under CC BY 4.0

aerial.licence: Auckland Central 0.06 m Urban Aerial Photos (2023): sourced from LINZ and licensed by Auckland Council for re-use under CC BY 4.0

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) within near_outline m of building 103's outline (the General Library, 109, stands 5-8 m to the south-south-west): centre = mean x/y of points higher than tower_above m: the four-storey block's low roof, 13.3-16.5 m up (the two-storey house at its west end, 8.7-11.5 m, is left out; a tree's crown over the house's north corner, classed as building, is not, and pulls the centre about 1 m west); axis = the bearing of most of the walls seen from above (axis_from walls), turned 90 deg (axis_across: the building is 50 m long and only its west end, the house's front, faces a street), pointing north-north-east; toStreet = the axis turned 90 deg toward street_side: west-north-west, to Princes Street.

streetview.pano_ids_note: the five Google panoramas that show the building whole or nearly (2026-10-22): three on Princes Street (2024-07, 48-49 m from the centre, 18-20 m from the house's front) see the house's front with the four-storey block behind it, one of them through a tree; two on the campus path east of it (2025-05, 33 and 48 m) see the block's east end, the second also its south-south-west side. Of the 53 panoramas within 120 m, the 13 Google ones within 70 m were looked at in a low-resolution probe (zoom 3, 88 tiles, bought through the ledger): of the other eight, one 27 m east stands 5 m from the east wall (its upper floors leave the picture), two on Princes Street see the house only past a bus or through trees, and five see the General Library or trees in front of it. User-contributed panoramas are not used.

ground_note: the LiDAR ground on the front path at the foot of the house's steps, 45.72-45.78 m (z 30-33 on the centre line); Princes Street is 45.6-45.8. The site falls away behind: 43.5 m along the long sides at the house's back (z 12), 42.4 at the block's east end and 41.2 at its north-north-east corner. The frame thresholds are above this ground (2.25 m lower than with the first, provisional 43.5, so the frame is the same).
